title: From Equity Pairs to Options Relative Value

research_map.caption: Research design: separate discovery of tradable relative value from allocation and subsequent extensions. The comparisons below retain their individual data and accounting conventions.

original_paper.caption: Ning and Lee (2024), Tables 3–4: arithmetic mean of reported daily Sharpe across ten pairs, formed in 2022 and traded in 2023. These published equity results use a different metric and setup from our annualized options results.
sources: Advanced Statistical Arbitrage with Reinforcement Learning.pdf

workflow.caption: Retained P25 strategy: rules propose the direction; the learner adjusts size. Orders use prior-close selected contracts on the next session. Positions hold to each leg’s expiry, except audited corporate exits.

smile_transfer.caption: Restricted 30D/90D formation comparison with learned positive sizing floors and matched proposal counts within each wing (P25 213, ATM 222, P75 55). P25 remains strongest at 30D; all three weaken at 90D. This restricted sample is distinct from the retained 608-proposal checkpoint.

signal_example.caption: AMD/NVDA, 2019: daily rolling selected-contract P25 IV spread and strictly prior rank boundaries. Green markers are signal dates; executions occur next session (12/13 August signals, 13/14 August fills). Gaps remain where either quote is unavailable; this is not the held-cohort mark series.

feature_ablations.caption: Original $345m research reference, identical 608 qualified proposals. Each block is added separately to the prior 27-input state. The retained variance-premium block reaches 1.006; most additional signals fail to improve the 0.962 learned baseline.

recency_search.caption: Monthly positive-floor sizing with alternative training windows, original $345m research reference. The retained 18-month model scores 0.962 versus 0.826 for the five-year reference. These are selected development results; shorter history does not improve monotonically.

allocation_model.caption: Retained contextual learner. Tree partitions map observable states to positive vega budgets; CEM searches allocations jointly. No Bellman continuation, learned exit, or direction reversal enters this checkpoint.

train_test.caption: Learned sizing improves each within-period benchmark. Training uses aggregated P&L paths and $0.65 commissions; walk-forward uses the funded ledger and $0.03 commissions. The levels are not directly comparable.

cash_relative_wealth.caption: Actual $10m funded portfolios, 2018–29 August 2025. Curves show 100 × (NAV / same-equity cash benchmark − 1), not total NAV returns. All controls share proposals and risk limits; sizing changes admission and inventory.

annual_results.caption: $10m learned strategy. Sharpe is annualized; calendar-period return above cash is not. The 2025 observation is partial through 29 August. Positive total funded returns can coexist with negative trading excess returns.

pair_contributions.caption: Five largest losing and winning pairs in the original $345m reference. Includes costs, hedges and dividends; excludes shared financing. This is retrospective attribution, not a rule for selecting or banning names.

management_results.caption: $10m live-admission replays. At 30D, 36-month management adds 0.027 Sharpe, while 18-month management reduces it. At 180D, conservative fitted Q adds 0.018. Algorithms, training schedules and strategies differ across panels; compare controls within each panel.

reversion_q.caption: Paper-inspired actual-P&L fitted Q, plain-P&L reward. The locked exit control preserves original accepted entries/counts (a counterfactual attribution control). Broad cases preserve all 17,967 cached evaluation candidates; 698/729 trades execute. Final model/execution v3 only; risk-penalized variants are separately reported and also fail to beat the checkpoint.

portfolio_results.caption: 2018–August 2025 including equal-weight warmup. Longer sleeves are the managed 180D and independently forecast 365D put strategies. Prior-performance allocation fails to beat equal weights. These are combinations of saved sleeve returns, not a new shared-inventory portfolio execution backtest.
